title: Not sure if it's new for anyone here, but I was mind blown!!
author: Infinite_Ad_9204
selftext:
This was made only with one prompt, no image reference, no 3d modeling tool  
Just prompt "Make a mech 3d model in three.js"

I'm impressed! This was made with fable 5.2

replies.author: Ok_Feedback4200
replies.body: Because it's using code to model. We are yet to create a real sculpting tool built for LLMs, not humans. There was a recent test by someone but it  felt more like a projection with fixes than real sculpting. We will solve this for sure, but it will take some time I think. Plus, even with the best agents and mechanical models, they can struggle with those too and you need lots of iterations or likely a very highly detailed prompt making sure all of those potential errors are accounted for. It also helps to break such modeling tasks into simpler quicker steps, mimicking the workflows of real studios, helps to get better results too. Start with blocking rough shapes, see how you like the silhouete first.. If you just ask it to create a realistic mechanical robot, it will produce a generic shit like in this post... Sure, it might look impressive knowing how fast this was made from a single prompt. But it's not anything usable if you care about the quality of your 3D work. Design itself always comes out as generic as it can get when you work from simple prompts like this. That's my take though as a 3D generalist who worked with 3D for a decade before these LLMs came out.

comments.author: 328amdev
comments.body: I find that most models, especially the recent releases, are really good at straightforward shapes and geometry but struggle still with organic shapes and curves. That's when I use other 3D modelling AI tools to cover for that weakness.
